headline: Automate grocery shopping with a Multimodal AI Nutrition Agent using LangGraph & GPT-4o
summary: An AI agent leverages GPT-4o Vision to analyze your fridge and LangGraph to orchestrate grocery orders via the Instacart API, ensuring you always have healthy ingredients.
details: Tired of staring at an empty fridge? This tutorial demonstrates building a high-performance Multimodal AI Nutritionist that goes beyond advice to take action. It monitors health data and automatically orders needed groceries.

The agent combines LangGraph for stateful orchestration, GPT-4o Vision for analyzing fridge contents, and OpenAI Function Calling to interface with the Instacart API. This setup creates a dynamic system for personalized wellness.

LangGraph is crucial for maintaining the agent's state, tracking user glucose levels, identified fridge ingredients, and the pending shopping list. This allows the agent to 'think,' 'see,' and 'act' based on real-time feedback.
GPT-4o Vision analyzes fridge photos, prompted to return a structured list of ingredients. It identifies what's fresh and what's missing, forming the basis for nutritional recommendations.
OpenAI Function Calling enables the agent to interact with the Instacart API. If the AI detects a need, such as low fiber-rich vegetables, it triggers an order through this tool.
This system offloads both the 'thinking' about what to eat and the 'doing' of buying food to an autonomous agent. It transforms AI into a personal assistant that actively improves healthy living.

headline: Databricks Serverless Compute cost team $14k in one weekend due to hidden heartbeat
summary: A team faced a $14,000 bill in a single weekend from Databricks Serverless Compute. A hidden heartbeat from a BI tool kept a large SQL warehouse active indefinitely, bypassing auto-stop settings.
details: The team received a PagerDuty alert indicating 80% of their monthly cloud spend was hit in 48 hours, resulting in a $14,000 bill from Databricks Serverless Compute. Their sql_warehouse_prod_v2 was consuming DBU excessively after a new pipeline deployment.

Initial investigations for runaway Python jobs or unusual Spark queries yielded no results. The "Auto-stop: 10 minutes" setting on the Serverless SQL Warehouse seemed bulletproof, but the warehouse wasn't truly idle.

The actual culprit was a hidden interaction with a Tableau BI tool. A connection string, configured with broad permissions, was performing a system.information_schema query on a heartbeat interval, which Databricks interpreted as an active query.

Because this heartbeat ping occurred every 8 minutes, it continuously reset the 10-minute auto-stop timer, preventing the "Large" size warehouse from ever becoming idle. This kept the expensive warehouse running constantly for a sub-millisecond metadata call.

The immediate fix involved killing the BI tool connection and manually setting the auto-stop to 1 minute. The team then redefined their warehouse configuration, splitting workloads into a "Serverless-Small" for dashboard heartbeats and a "Large" for ad-hoc queries.

They also updated the BI tool's connection string to target a specific Unity Catalog schema, avoiding broad information_schema scans. Custom tags were implemented for better cost isolation in billing exports.

The incident led to new policies: strict warehouse sizing (no production warehouse larger than "Medium" without documented exemption and cost-estimate checks) and moving away from generic service principals.
The key lesson was that while Serverless removes node management, session lifecycle management remains crucial. Trusting "Serverless is magic" marketing proved costly.
